# Brisa Framework 🌬️

> Minimalist, zero-dependency, 100% pure Go (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) desktop application micro-framework built around the **REPR Design Pattern (Request-Endpoint-Response)** for IPC commands and featuring a built-in **GNOME 50 / GTK4 Libadwaita UI Kit** (`/brisa/adwaita.css`) with OS-governed Light/Dark synchronization and an interactive D-Spy style IPC Inspector (`/brisa/inspector`).

This document is the definitive specification, API reference, and rulebook for the **Brisa** desktop framework in Go. Strictly follow the signatures, struct tags, CSS classes, and constraints documented here.

---

## 1. Overview & Core Philosophy

- **Module & Import**: `github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa`
  - Import **only** `github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa` in application code. All core types (`App`, `Config`, `WindowConfig`, `Window`, `WindowState`, `Context`, `Command`, `CommandGroup`, `CommandDoc`, `CommandSchema`, `FieldSchema`, `InspectorSpec`, `DispatchResult`, `HandlerFunc`, `MiddlewareFunc`, `EventHandler`, `Map`, `Empty`, `RPCError`, `ErrorResponse`, `ValidationError`, `Validator`, `ContextValidator`, `Store`, `StoreOptions`, `Dialog`, `FileFilter`, `FileDialogOptions`, `MessageDialogOptions`, `NotificationOptions`, `Clipboard`) are re-exported on the root `brisa` package.
- **Zero External Dependencies**: `go.mod` contains zero third-party packages. Built 100% on the Go standard library (`net/http`, `embed`, `reflect`, `encoding/json`, `crypto/aes`, `crypto/cipher`, `crypto/sha1`, `crypto/sha256`, `log/slog`, `sync`).
- **100% Pure Go (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) & Deno Desktop / Lorca Engine Model**: Unlike Electron (which bundles 150–250 MB of Chromium + Node.js per app) or CGO WebView frameworks (which require `gcc` and C headers), Brisa produces a ~5–8 MB single binary and reuses the user's existing OS browser engine (Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi discovered via `brisa.LocateBrowser()`) in an isolated, chromeless `--app` window controlled via a pure-Go RFC 6455 WebSocket client (`core/cdp.go`) speaking Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).
- **OS-Governed GNOME 50 / GTK4 Libadwaita UI**: Brisa serves `/brisa/adwaita.css` and automatically synchronizes Light/Dark mode strictly from the operating system (`stdbuf -oL gsettings monitor org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme` on Linux/GNOME, `AppleInterfaceStyle` on macOS, `AppsUseLightTheme` on Windows, and native `@media (prefers-color-scheme)`). Do **not** build manual/internal theme switchers in Brisa apps; let the OS govern the theme.
- **Go Version**: Requires **Go 1.26+**.

---

## 2. Application Bootstrap & Configuration

`brisa.New` accepts a single `brisa.Config` struct:

```go
package main

import (
	"embed"
	"log"

	"github.com/carlosxfelipe/brisa"
)

//go:embed ui
var uiAssets embed.FS

func main() {
	app := brisa.New(brisa.Config{
		AppID:              "com.example.studio", // Default: "com.brisa.app" (used for OS config dir)
		Title:              "Brisa Studio",       // Default: "Brisa Desktop App"
		Version:            "1.0.0",              // Default: "1.0.0"
		Description:        "Desktop app built with Brisa REPR IPC",
		Addr:               "127.0.0.1:0",        // Default: "127.0.0.1:0" (ephemeral loopback port)
		Assets:             uiAssets,             // Optional fs.FS / embed.FS
		AssetsSubDir:       "ui",                 // Optional subdirectory inside Assets
		IndexHTML:          "",                   // Optional inline HTML when Assets is nil
		DevServerURL:       "",                   // Optional reverse proxy for Vite/frontend dev server
		InspectorURL:       "/brisa/inspector",   // Default: "/brisa/inspector" (set "-" to disable)
		Theme:              brisa.ThemeAdwaita,   // Default: brisa.ThemeAdwaita
		DisableAdwaitaCSS:  false,                // Default: false (auto-injects /brisa/adwaita.css)
		DisableCSRFToken:   false,                // Default: false (enforces X-Brisa-Token on /brisa/rpc)
		SilenceTagWarnings: false,                // Set true to suppress non-fatal startup validation tag warnings
		Window: brisa.WindowConfig{
			Title:       "Brisa Studio",
			Width:       1120,  // Default: 1080
			Height:      740,   // Default: 720
			X:           0,     // Optional initial X coordinate
			Y:           0,     // Optional initial Y coordinate
			Fullscreen:  false, // Start in fullscreen mode
			Maximized:   false, // Start maximized
			Headless:    false, // Set true for CI / automated tests without a display server
			BrowserPath: "",    // Optional custom path to Chromium/Chrome/Edge/Brave binary
			CustomFlags: nil,   // Optional extra Chromium CLI flags
		},
		Store: brisa.StoreOptions{
			Path:          "",               // Default: os.UserConfigDir()/<AppID>/store.json
			EncryptionKey: "my-secret-key",  // Optional: enables AES-256-GCM encryption at rest
			MemoryOnly:    false,            // Set true for in-memory ephemeral storage (e.g. unit tests)
		},
	})

	// Global Middlewares
	app.Use(brisa.Recover(), brisa.Logger())

	log.Fatal(app.Run())
}
```

### Lifecycle Hooks & Methods on `*brisa.App`

- `app.OnStartup(func(ctx context.Context) error)`: Executed before the loopback server and window launch.
- `app.OnReady(func(app *brisa.App))`: Executed once the loopback server is bound and the desktop window is launched.
- `app.OnBeforeClose(func(app *brisa.App) bool)`: Called before shutdown; returning `false` aborts closing.
- `app.OnShutdown(func(app *brisa.App))`: Cleanup hook executed when the app exits.
- `app.Start(ctx context.Context) error`: Non-blocking start (binds server, launches window, starts OS theme watcher).
- `app.Run() error`: Blocking start that waits until the desktop window closes or `os.Interrupt`/`syscall.SIGTERM` is received.
- `app.Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error`: Gracefully closes the window and shuts down the loopback HTTP server.
- `app.Dispatch(ctx context.Context, command string, payload any) (*brisa.DispatchResult, error)`: Executes any registered IPC command directly in Go memory (runs full middleware + validation pipeline).
- `app.ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)`: Implements `http.Handler` for `httptest`.

---

## 3. The REPR Pattern for Desktop IPC

Every desktop IPC operation is organized into three components:
1. **Request DTO (`TReq`)**: Input struct with `json`, `validate`, `msg`, `doc`, and `example` tags (use `brisa.Empty` when no input is needed).
2. **Endpoint**: Handler function `func(ctx *brisa.Context, req TReq) (TRes, error)` or struct implementing `brisa.Endpoint[TReq, TRes]`.
3. **Response DTO (`TRes`)**: Output struct or value serialized as JSON (use `brisa.Empty` when returning no data).

### 3.1 Functional REPR Command (`brisa.Bind`)

```go
type CreateTaskRequest struct {
	Title    string `json:"title" doc:"Task title" example:"Ship Flatpak" validate:"required,min=3,max=80"`
	Priority string `json:"priority" doc:"Urgency" example:"high" validate:"required,oneof=low,medium,high"`
}

type Task struct {
	ID       string `json:"id"`
	Title    string `json:"title"`
	Priority string `json:"priority"`
}

tasks := app.Group("tasks").Tags("Tasks")

brisa.Bind(tasks, "create", func(ctx *brisa.Context, req CreateTaskRequest) (Task, error) {
	return Task{ID: "tsk_1", Title: req.Title, Priority: req.Priority}, nil
}).
	Summary("Create a new task").
	Description("Validates input declaratively and persists to the encrypted store.").
	Middleware(brisa.Timeout(5 * time.Second))
```

### 3.2 Struct-Based REPR Endpoint (`brisa.BindEndpoint`)

```go
type CreateTaskEndpoint struct{}

func (e *CreateTaskEndpoint) Handle(ctx *brisa.Context, req CreateTaskRequest) (Task, error) {
	return Task{ID: "tsk_1", Title: req.Title, Priority: req.Priority}, nil
}

brisa.BindEndpoint(tasks, "create", &CreateTaskEndpoint{}).Summary("Create a new task")
```

### 3.3 Reflected Service Struct (`brisa.BindService`)

Automatically reflects exported methods on a struct and registers them as `<namespace>.<camelCaseMethod>`:

```go
type SystemService struct{}

func (s *SystemService) Info() (brisa.Map, error) {
	return brisa.Map{"os": runtime.GOOS}, nil
}

// Registers "system.info"
brisa.BindService(app, "system", &SystemService{})
```

Supported method signatures on a service struct:
- `func(ctx *brisa.Context, req TReq) (TRes, error)`
- `func(req TReq) (TRes, error)`
- `func(ctx *brisa.Context) (TRes, error)`
- `func() (TRes, error)`

---

## 4. Declarative Validation (`validate` & `msg` Tags)

Validation runs automatically before the command handler executes. Invalid `validate` rule names panic at registration time (`validation.CheckTags`) so typos fail fast at startup.

| Rule | Description | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `required` | Rejects zero values (`""`, whitespace-only string, `0`, `false`, `nil` pointer/slice/map). | `validate:"required"` |
| `min=N` | Minimum numeric value, UTF-8 rune count (`string`), or item count (`slice`). | `validate:"min=3"` |
| `max=N` | Maximum numeric value, UTF-8 rune count (`string`), or item count (`slice`). | `validate:"max=80"` |
| `len=N` | Exact UTF-8 rune count (`string`) or item count (`slice`/`map`). | `validate:"len=4"` |
| `oneof=a,b,c` | Value must match one of the listed options (comma or space separated). | `validate:"oneof=low,medium,high"` |
| `email` | Valid email address (`net/mail`). | `validate:"email"` |
| `url` | Valid URL with scheme and host (`net/url`). | `validate:"url"` |
| `uuid` | Valid RFC 4122 UUID. | `validate:"uuid"` |
| `nowarn` | Suppresses startup warning when `required` is placed on a non-pointer numeric/bool field. | `validate:"required,nowarn"` |

### Custom Validation Messages & Interfaces

- **Custom `msg` / `message` Tag**:
  - Single fallback message: `msg:"Title is invalid"`
  - Per-rule messages separated by `|`: `msg:"required:Title is required|min:Title must have at least 3 chars"`
- **Custom `Validator` / `ContextValidator` Interfaces**:
  - Implement `Validate() error` or `Validate(ctx *brisa.Context) error` on the request struct for cross-field validation; errors are added under `_general`.

---

## 5. `brisa.Context` & Error Handling

Inside any command handler or middleware:
- `ctx.Context() context.Context` / `ctx.WithContext(c)`
- `ctx.Command() string`: Name of the invoked command (e.g. `"tasks.create"`).
- `ctx.RequestID() string` / `ctx.SetRequestID(id)`
- `ctx.Set(key, val)` / `ctx.Get(key) (any, bool)` / `ctx.MustGet(key) any`
- `ctx.Emit(event string, data any)`: Broadcasts a real-time event to Go listeners and all connected frontend windows via SSE.
- `ctx.Store() *brisa.Store`: Accesses the persistent local key-value/JSON store (`Get`, `GetString`, `GetInt`, `GetBool`, `Set`, `Delete`, `Clear`, `Keys`, `All`).
- `ctx.Window() *brisa.Window`: Controls the desktop window (`SetTitle`, `SetSize`, `SetPosition`, `Minimize`, `Maximize`, `Restore`, `SetFullscreen`, `Eval`, `Close`, `State`).
- `ctx.Dialog() *brisa.Dialog`: Opens native OS dialogs (`Info`, `Warn`, `Error`, `Confirm`, `OpenFile`, `OpenMultipleFiles`, `OpenDirectory`, `SaveFile`).
- `ctx.Clipboard() *brisa.Clipboard`: Reads/writes system clipboard text (`ReadText`, `WriteText`).
- `ctx.Notify(brisa.NotificationOptions) error`: Sends a native OS desktop notification.
- `brisa.NewError(status int, code, message string) *brisa.RPCError`: Returns a structured error with HTTP-like status and machine-readable code.

---

## 6. Built-in Desktop UI Kit & Themes

Unless `DisableAdwaitaCSS: true` is set, Brisa automatically injects its built-in stylesheet (`/brisa/adwaita.css` or `/brisa/theme.css`) into `index.html`. All HTML layout and component classes work identically across all themes.

- **Configuring a Theme (`Config.Theme` or `app.SetTheme(...)`)**:
  - `brisa.ThemeAdwaita` (`"adwaita"`, default): GNOME 50 / GTK4 Libadwaita (`#3584e4`, `"Cantarell"`, `9px`/`12px` radii).
  - `brisa.ThemeUbuntu` (`"ubuntu"` / `"yaru"`): Canonical Ubuntu Yaru GTK4 (`#e95420`, `"Ubuntu Sans"`, `6px`/`8px` radii, `/brisa/ubuntu.css`).
  - `brisa.ThemePlasma` (`"plasma"` / `"kde"` / `"breeze"`): KDE Plasma Breeze (`#3daee9`, `"Noto Sans"`, `5px`/`6px` radii, `/brisa/plasma.css`).
  - `brisa.ThemeMacOS` (`"macos"` / `"darwin"` / `"aqua"` / `"mac"`): Apple macOS (`#0a84ff` / `#007aff`, `"SF Pro"`, `8px`/`11px` radii, `/brisa/macos.css`).
  - `brisa.ThemeWindows` (`"windows"` / `"win11"` / `"fluent"` / `"winui"`): Microsoft Windows 11 Fluent / WinUI 3 (`#0067c0` / `#60cdff`, `"Segoe UI Variable"`, `4px`/`8px` radii, `/brisa/windows.css`).
- **OS-Governed Color Scheme**: Never add manual theme-toggle buttons in the UI. Light/Dark mode is strictly governed by the OS (`:root` dark tokens + `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` + `:root[data-os-theme="light"]` updated in `<1ms` via `stdbuf -oL gsettings monitor org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`).
- **Standard Layout Classes**:
  - `.adw-split-view`: 2-column grid (`256px` `.adw-sidebar` + `1fr` `.adw-content-view`).
  - `.adw-sidebar`, `.adw-sidebar-header`, `.adw-nav-list`, `.adw-nav-row` (`.active`).
  - `.adw-content-view`, `.adw-toolbar`, `.adw-page`, `.adw-clamp` (`max-width: 680px` centered container).
  - `.adw-group`, `.adw-group-title`, `.adw-group-desc`, `.boxed-list` (`border-radius: 12px` card list).
  - `.adw-row` (`.activatable`), `.adw-row-text`, `.adw-row-title`, `.adw-row-subtitle`, `.adw-row-suffix`.
  - `.adw-entry-input`: Borderless inline GTK4 entry input inside an `.adw-row`.
- **Unified GTK4 Button & Dropdown Geometry (`34px` height, `9px` radius)**:
  - `.gtk-btn` (and `<button>`): `height: 34px; min-height: 34px; padding: 0 14px; border-radius: 9px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600;`
  - Modifiers: `.suggested-action` (Adwaita Blue `#3584e4`), `.destructive-action`, `.flat`, `.circular` (`34px × 34px` icon button), `.pill` (`height: 38px; border-radius: 999px`).
  - `.gtk-dropdown` (and `<select>`): `appearance: none; height: 34px; border-radius: 9px; padding: 0 32px 0 14px;` with embedded SVG `pan-down-symbolic` chevron.

---

## 7. Frontend JavaScript SDK (`/brisa/sdk.js`)

Automatically injected into `index.html` as `window.brisa`:
- `await brisa.invoke("tasks.create", { title: "Ship v1", priority: "high" })`
- `await brisa.call.tasks.create({ title: "Ship v1", priority: "high" })`
- `await brisa.batch([{ command: "tasks.list", payload: {} }])`
- `const unsub = brisa.on("system:telemetry", (data) => { ... })`
- `brisa.once("tasks:created", (data) => { ... })`
- `await brisa.emit("client:ready", { ts: Date.now() })`
- `await brisa.window.setTitle("New Title")` / `setSize(w, h)` / `setPosition(x, y)` / `minimize()` / `maximize()` / `restore()` / `setFullscreen(true)` / `close()` / `state()`
- `await brisa.dialog.info(title, msg)` / `warn(title, msg)` / `error(title, msg)` / `confirm(title, msg)` / `openFile(opts)` / `openMultipleFiles(opts)` / `openDirectory(opts)` / `saveFile(opts)`
- `await brisa.clipboard.writeText("text")` / `await brisa.clipboard.readText()`
- `await brisa.store.get("key")` / `set("key", val)` / `delete("key")` / `keys()` / `all()` / `clear()`
- `await brisa.notify({ title: "Done", body: "Completed" })`
- `await brisa.openExternal("https://example.com")`
